muc.title: Breaking down like human teams
muc.text: Multi-agent is powerful, but it also breaks down in ways very much like human teams.

muc.title: A game of telephone
muc.text: Type one: a game of telephone. The request passes through three agents, and each summary loses a little. By the end, the result has drifted from the original idea.

muc.title: Errors add up
muc.text: Type two: errors add up, called error compounding. Each step is ninety-five percent right, which sounds great. But chain ten steps together, and the whole thing is only about sixty percent right.

muc.title: Expensive and slow
muc.text: Type three: expensive and slow. Fifteen times the tokens, for a job one agent could have done.

muc.title: Can it be split?
muc.text: So before using multi-agent, ask one question: can this job be split into independent parts? If yes, use multi-agent. If not, one good agent with enough tools is enough.

muc.title: The whole series in one picture
muc.text: The whole series in short: AI uses tool calling to get things done. MCP is the shared socket. Install servers carefully. And multi-agent splits the work, when the job is big enough.

muc.title: Ask before calling the whole team
muc.text: Next time you're about to use deep research or multi-agent, ask the split question first. For small jobs, just ask directly. It's faster and cheaper.

muc.title: Who watches the AI team?
muc.text: Multi-agent is running for real now. Who keeps an eye on it? Watch the next series: Behind the scenes of an AI system.
